articles.title: Cody Rhodes shares how wrestling complicated his relationship with late father Dusty Rhodes and brother Dustin Rhodes
articles.summary: WWE News: WWE star Cody Rhodes has recently provided us with a glimpse of his personal life, sharing how wrestling had complicated his relationship with his lat.
articles.body: WWE star Cody Rhodes has recently provided us with a glimpse of his personal life, sharing how wrestling had complicated his relationship with his late father Dusty Rhodes and brother Dustin Rhodes. Cody Rhodes is the son of Dusty Rhodes, a legendary figure in WWE, and his half-brother, Dustin Rhodes, is also a big name in the wrestling world.He has recently shared a personal anecdote regarding his relationship with his late father, Dusty Rhodes, acknowledging that the legendary wrestler's demanding wrestling career created a distance within the family.Rhodes joined wrestling holding the hands of Dusty Rhodes. He joined the company in April 2022, performing on the SmackDown brand. From 2016 until 2019, Rhodes wrestled on the independent circuit and New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), and Ring of Honor (ROH) under the mononym Cody. He is also known for co-founding and serving as executive vice president and wrestler with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) from 2019 until 2022.Cody Rhodes offers a candid look at his family relations with Dusty Rhodes and Dustin RhodesCody Rhodes offers a candid look at his family relations with Dusty Rhodes and Dustin Rhodes, acknowledging that the legendary wrestler’s demanding career created distance within the family. Speaking recently with Santino Marella on What Do You Wanna Talk About? Cody discussed how the wrestling business affected his family while reflecting on his relationship with his older half-brother, Dustin Rhodes.According to Cody, he and Dustin did not grow up together in the traditional sense, with their 16-year age gap contributing to their different childhood experiences. Cody explained that much of the brothers’ relationship effectively played out in the public eye.Speaking to Marella, The American Nightmare stated, “One of the things, though, that I found before I ever had kids, and it’s largely now present as well that I do wrestling can tear the you can take the family away from each other.”“But in my case, a lot of my family lived their life on screen. So people don’t realize as far as my brother and I didn’t grow up together. We didn’t have Thanksgivings together. We didn’t; the age gap was too much. Our, what’s the age gap? Sixteen years. Wow. Us being brothers was on television. Was on TV.”He further threw light on Dusty’s relationship with his brother Dustin Rhodes. Cody stated that Dustin’s relationship was more painful. Cody brought up Dusty’s famous “The View Never Changes” promo with Dustin, which he considers one of the greatest wrestling promos ever delivered. But, sadly, it was a shoot and was not made for television. ”So Dusty has a promo with Dustin, the ‘View Never Changes’ promo. I think it’s the best promo of all time. But the sad part, it’s a shoot. You know, like that’s a that’s a tricky thing," he added.Cody further acknowledged that he received a different upbringing from his father than Dustin did. He recalled traveling with Dusty and being able to experience the wrestling world alongside him, something his older brother did not have.However, the difficult relationship between Dusty Rhodes and Dustin Rhodes eventually improved and the family was able to reconnect.The American Nightmare also shared his own experiences with Dusty influencing the way he approaches fatherhood. Rather than keeping his children completely removed from wrestling, Cody said he is comfortable with them sharing parts of his career and appearing on television.It is important to note that Cody Rhodes and his wife, Brandi Rhodes, have two daughters together. They are Liberty Iris Runnels and Leilani Ella Runnels.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Can Nico Daws become the New Jersey Devils’ No. 1 goalie? Martin Brodeur believes he deserves the chance
articles.summary: NHL News: The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserv.
articles.body: The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.Why does Martin Brodeur believe Nico Daws deserves a chance?According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years. We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”Nico Daws has already shown the New Jersey Devils what he can doWhile Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting
articles.summary: International Sports News: For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and.
articles.body: For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter.” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood?Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last. Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mitch Evans tops London E-Prix FP1, Pascal Wehrlein finishes third and Jake Dennis fifth
articles.summary: Formula - E News: The Formula E World Championship finale kickstarted in the UK with the London E-Prix on Friday. The first free practice, FP1, was held in the evening .
articles.body: The Formula E World Championship finale kickstarted in the UK with the London E-Prix on Friday. The first free practice, FP1, was held in the evening and had Jaguar TCS Racing driver Mitch Evans topping the timesheets. Andretti’s Jake Dennis, who is just two points ahead of Evans in the title race, finished fifth in the practice race. The main races will take place on Saturday and Sunday at the London ExCeL Circuit.2026 London E-Prix FP1 resultsJaguar TCS Racing gave Evans a pleasant surprise by giving him a special helmet with the message “To a decade of memories” written on it. Graphic images from Evans’ Formula E victories also featured on the helmet. The Kiwi driver would be leaving the team at the end of the season and this is his last race weekend with the team in London.Evans was followed by Mahindra Racing driver Nyck De Vries in second in FP1. Porsche driver Pascal Wehrlein, who is just five points behind Dennis and stands third in title race, finished third in the practice race. DS Penske driver Taylor Barnard took the fourth position followed by Dennis in fifth. Dennis had bit of a moment on track but he was able to keep clear of the barriers and was able to return to the track.Jaguar TCS Racing driver Antonio Felix Da Costa finished sixth, followed by Mahindra Racing’s Edoardo Mortara in seventh and Porsche driver Nico Muller in eighth. Envision Racing’s Sebastien Buemi was ninth while Citroen Racing’s Nick Cassidy was tenth in FP1. After the season finale, Buemi will also be leaving Envision Racing along with teammate Joel Eriksson.More highlights from London E-PrixAmong the high-profile audience was Oliver Rowland’s toddler son, Hennie. A video of him looking elated on watching his dad on TV while wearing headphones was shared on X.The London E-Prix marks the finale race weekend of the Formula E World Championship before the season 12 comes to a close. The new season will begin in December with the arrival of the GEN4 car.The result of the Drivers’ Championship and the Teams’ Championship will also be decided this weekend. Dennis leads the title race, followed by Mitch Evans and Pascal Wehrlein in close proximity. Reigning champion Oliver Rowland is fourth, followed by Edoardo Mortara.The Round 16 race will start on Saturday at 3:05pm (7:35pm IST). The Round 17 race will also take place at the same time on Sunday, marking the curtain downer on the season.Also read: 2026 London E-Prix schedule: Round 16 and 17 timings, how to watch Formula E Championship finale and moreGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "We've always tried to protect our children": Victoria Beckham reflects on parenting with David Beckham amid feud with Brooklyn Beckham
articles.summary: International Sports News: David Beckham, the football legend, and his wife, Victoria Beckham, have been in the public eye for close to three decades due to their successful car.
articles.body: David Beckham, the football legend, and his wife, Victoria Beckham, have been in the public eye for close to three decades due to their successful careers. While the two have always been united when it came to challenges in their lives, David Beckham and Victoria Beckham are still dealing with a public feud concerning their oldest son, Brooklyn Beckam, and their daughter in law, Nicola Peltz.David Beckham’s wife Victoria Beckham on wanting to “protect” their family amid Brooklyn Beckham’s accusationsIn a recent interview with the Wall Street Journal, fashion icon and former pop star Victoria Beckham opened up about parenthood as she said, "I think that we've always - we love our children so much.Victoria Beckham added, "We've always tried to be the best parents that we can be. And you know, we've been in the public eye for more than 30 years right now, and all we've ever tried to do is protect our children and love our children."Contrary to Victoria Beckham’s comments about parenthood, Brooklyn Beckham has not backed down from the controversial accusations he made against them.For the unversed, a few months ago, in January 2026 Brooklyn Beckham took to his social media to make a post that read as, "My parents have been trying endlessly to ruin my relationship since before my wedding, and it hasn't stopped.”The post added, “My mum cancelled making Nicola's dress in the eleventh hour despite how excited she was to wear her design, forcing her to urgently find a new dress. Weeks before our big day, my parents repeatedly pressured and attempted to bribe me into signing away the rights to my name, which would have affected me, my wife, and our future children.”Both David Beckham and his wife, Victoria Beckham, have refused to comment on Brooklyn Beckham’s accusations.David Beckham reflects on parenthood amid drama with Brooklyn BeckhamWhile David Beckham has remained distant from Brooklyn Beckham in public, he has spoken about parenthood.The Manchester United legend said, “I would like to say that I brought my children up with the same values as what my Dad and Mum taught me and my sisters. “My kids are very polite. My kids are very well-mannered.”The 50 year old football icon added, “My kids are humble, and they all have the same values as what I have and my wife has. That’s the proudest thing that we have as parents, in all honesty.”He continued, “Family has always been important, and the greatest thing [Victoria Beckham] has ever given me is my four children.”Over the last few months, David Beckham and Victoria Beckham have remained united and have tried to focus on their respective careers and life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: International Sports News: Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever failed to survive against Paige Bueckers’ Dallas Wings. Bueckers and co. handed the Indiana Fever a 91-85 loss. The resu.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever failed to survive against Paige Bueckers’ Dallas Wings. Bueckers and co. handed the Indiana Fever a 91-85 loss. The result ended Indiana's five-game winning streak, with Kelsey Mitchell's 37 points unable to prevent the Fever from falling on the road.The matchup featured two of the WNBA's biggest young stars, but it was Arike Ogunbowale and Jessica Shepard who made the bigger scoring impact for Dallas. Ogunbowale had 32 points, while Shepard added a career-high 26.Caitlin Clark vs. Paige Bueckers showdown: Wings beat FeverThe Dallas Wings held off the Indiana Fever 91-85, ending a five-game run that had pushed Indiana to 24-13. The Fever now travel to New York to face the Liberty on Saturday night.Indiana had to lean heavily on Mitchell, who scored 37 points and extended her remarkable streak to 21 consecutive games with at least 20 points, a new WNBA record. Aliyah Boston added 14 points and nine rebounds, while Makayla Timpson posted 11 points and 12 rebounds.Clark's nine assists were important in keeping Indiana's offense moving, but the Fever received little production beyond their main contributors. Indiana's bench scored only four points.Dallas had more balance. Ogunbowale's 32 points led all Wings scorers, while Shepard's 26-point performance marked a career high. Awak Kuier added 11 points, eight rebounds and seven blocked shots, giving Dallas a major defensive presence around the basket.The game was tied 42-42 at halftime. Clark had five points and six assists at the break, while Bueckers had five points. Shepard had already scored 22 for Dallas, and Kuier had six points along with five blocks.The game remained tight into the second half. Dallas led 61-56 with 1:29 left in the third quarter after Ogunbowale scored 12 straight points for the Wings. She eventually finished with 32, providing the late offensive push Dallas needed.How many points did Caitlin Clark score against the Wings?Caitlin Clark scored 10 points in 35 minutes against Dallas, finishing with nine assists and four rebounds. She shot 4-for-15 from the field, including 2-for-8 from three-point range, and went 0-for-1 at the free-throw line.PlayerPosMINPTSFG3PTFTREBASTSTLBLKTOPFCaitlin ClarkG35104-152-80-1491134Clark also recorded one steal and one block, while committing three turnovers and four personal fouls. Her scoring was modest, but her nine assists reflected her continued role as one of Indiana's primary creators.Clark's presence has also remained a major factor beyond the court. The Fever's recent games have produced some of the WNBA's strongest television audiences.Indiana's Aug. 14 win over Dallas averaged 1.62 million viewers on ION, becoming the most-watched WNBA game in the network's history. The game peaked at 2.2 million viewers. Two days later, the Fever's overtime win over Atlanta averaged 2.58 million viewers on ESPN and peaked at 4 million.How many points did Paige Bueckers score against the Wings?Paige Bueckers scored 13 points in 35 minutes, adding eight assists and six rebounds in the Wings' victory. She went 5-for-16 from the field, missed both three-point attempts and shot 3-for-4 from the free-throw line.PlayerPosMINPTSFG3PTFTREBASTSTLBLKTOPFPaige BueckersG35135-160-23-4680004Bueckers also committed four fouls but did not record a steal, block or turnover. Her scoring output trailed Ogunbowale and Shepard, yet her eight assists and six rebounds gave Dallas another way to control the game.The result added another chapter to the growing spotlight around Clark and Bueckers, two players who have helped drive interest in the WNBA. articles.title: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand end India’s 15-year wait, assure World Championships medal
articles.summary: Badminton News: India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a World Championships medal after producing a superb comeback victory over China’s Jia Yi Fan and Z.
articles.body: India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a World Championships medal after producing a superb comeback victory over China’s Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian in the women’s doubles quarterfinals on Friday.The unseeded Indian pair fought for 69 minutes before overcoming their Chinese opponents 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 to book their place in the last four. The victory guarantees Treesa and Gayatri at least a bronze medal at the championships.Their achievement is particularly significant for Indian women’s doubles badminton. The country’s last World Championships medal in the event came in 2011, when Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa claimed bronze in London.Backed by strong home support, Treesa and Gayatri recovered from a slow start and gradually took control of the contest. After dropping the opening game, the Indians sharpened their attacking play, finding greater success with their smashes and producing cleaner work around the net.The semifinal appearance marks another major milestone for a pair that has already enjoyed success on the international circuit. Treesa and Gayatri reached the All England Open semifinals in consecutive years in 2022 and 2023. They also won bronze at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and broke into the world’s top 10 at the beginning of last year.Their progress was interrupted earlier this year when Treesa suffered a serious ankle injury during training ahead of the Asia Badminton Championships and Uber Cup.The injury occurred when Treesa accidentally stepped on Gayatri’s foot during practice and twisted her ankle. An MRI subsequently revealed two high-grade muscle tears and two ligament tears, forcing her into a lengthy rehabilitation programme.The pair eventually began their comeback at the Indonesia Open before competing at the US Open. They then won the Philippine International Challenge earlier this month, providing further evidence that they were returning to their best.Now, that comeback has reached its biggest moment yet, with Treesa and Gayatri assured of a place on the World Championships podium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian lawn bowlers ready for New Zealand challenge after landmark year
articles.summary: KOLKATA: It has been a good year for Indian lawn bowls.
articles.body: KOLKATA: It has been a good year for Indian lawn bowls. Putul Sonowal won bronze at the Champion of Champions tournament, India claimed four gold medals at the Asian Championships, and recently added a bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open.Perhaps more significantly, the Bowling Federation of India (BFI) received recognition from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the governing body for lawn bowls in the country. It was a major boost for the sport as it looks to build towards the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.Before that, however, the focus is on the Test series against New Zealand, scheduled for Nov 16, 17 and 18 in Auckland as part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two nations.Each Test will comprise five matches: men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2. India will be represented by Dinesh Kumar, Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh.Speaking about the opportunity, Dinesh, a five-time CWG participant, said: “Getting the opportunity to represent India in the Test series is a great moment for us. We are going there with the aim of delivering a strong performance.”Having trained together since 2008, Dinesh and Sunil have enjoyed a remarkable journey. The Ranchi-based duo now hopes to make the most of international competition as Indian lawn bowls continues to gain momentum on the global stage.“We are travelling regularly and gaining experience against some of the world’s best players. Every match becomes a learning opportunity. Even when we lose, we understand where we need to improve. Competing against experienced international players accelerates our development,” said Sunil, who partnered Reshma to win bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open earlier this month.The medal was a particularly significant achievement for Reshma, who was previously a 1500m runner but switched sports in 2023 after struggling with injuries. She is now eager to make the most of her upcoming tour to New Zealand.“Things are progressing well, my game is improving, and I am determined to take full advantage of every opportunity that comes my way,” said the youngster.While the players are pleased with the progress the sport has made in recent years, they believe India would benefit from hosting more invitational tournaments, similar to those regularly staged in established lawn bowls nations.BFI president Ravi Bengani shares that ambition. Having previously expressed confidence that India can challenge for as many as four gold medals at the 2030 Commonwealth Games, he is focused on creating more opportunities for players to gain exposure at the highest level.“Besides participating in international tournaments, we have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani had said.For now, however, the immediate challenge lies in Auckland, where India’s lawn bowlers will look to cap a landmark year by making a statement against New Zealand.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Littler produces triple-bullseye checkout on way to last 16 despite first ever defeat at Grand Slam of Darts
articles.summary: Luke Littler took out 150 with three bullseyes in the eighth leg of his match; Despite the showstopping moment, he lost to Niels Zonneveld; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports with the final taking place on Sunday November 22
articles.body:
The reigning champion needed to win just three legs to make it through from a tough Group A and after going 1-0 down, he rattled off three in a row to ensure his title defence continues.

The highlight of the match came in the eighth leg as Zonneveld was waiting to come for a second match dart on 20 and Littler was on 150.

Not only did Littler take it out but he did it in the most sublime style with three bullseyes, asking his family in the crowd beforehand if he 'should do it'. With the answer of yes, he nailed all three and sent the Wolverhampton crowd wild.

Although Littler had come up with one of the greatest finishes you can see, Zonneveld held his nerve to take the match and take a piece of history home as the first player ever to beat Littler at this major. He was eliminated alongside Beau Greaves in Group A.

Asked whether he thought Littler going that route with the match still on the line was disrespectful, Zonneveld said: "I don't think it was disrespectful because I was 4-3 up, he was already through so could go for the three bullseyes.

"It was brilliant, of course. But for me it was really tough because of the group, but I don't see it as disrespect."

In the last 16, 'The Nuke' will take on Jermaine Wattimena . Wattimena won a straight shootout with Alan Soutar and progressed from Group B off the back of eight missed match darts from the Scotsman, finally taking the contest and a place in the last 16 on D8.

The other big moment of the night came in Group E in which fourth seed Gerwyn Price was clinical in a 5-2 victory over Sebastian Bialecki but the win came with some controversy.

In the fourth leg, it seemed like Price took out 135 for a hold of throw, but he had in fact taken out 145 due to a miscalculation from referee Charlie Corstophine.

Price went the route of T19, T16, and D20 and after his first dart at T19, he asked the referee what was remaining and was told 88.

However, he in fact needed 78 which led to the error of him being awarded the leg despite busting his throw.

Next up, he faces Ryan Searle who rattled off five legs in a row for a 5-2 victory over Andrew Gilding in the straight shootout in Group F.

What else happened on Monday at the Grand Slam?

Cameron Menzies is through from Group D and eliminated Stephen Bunting in the process with a 5-2 victory in the penultimate Monday match.

His 103.39 average was too much to handle and in a composed showing in a pressurised straight shootout, he clinched a brilliant 144 finish and then took the contest with a 135 checkout on the bull.

In the last 16, he faces Kevin Doets who blew Tommy Morris away with a scintillating 5-1 victory to take top spot in Group C and finished the match in style with a 121 checkout on the bullseye.

Eighth seed Josh Rock had already been eliminated after two defeats and despite Morris impressing earlier in the tournament, he could not find his rhythm and Doets punished to make it into the next round on his Grand Slam debut.

Fifth-seed Jonny Clayton was already out of the running in Group G and Rob Cross took full advantage and progressed with a 5-1 victory over Anton Ostlund.

With the doubles troubling Ostlund, Cross made sure to make his opportunities count and took out five of the six legs played for a clinical win.

Cross now faces a mouthwatering clash against Niko Springer who came out on top against Wessel Nijman in what was a tussle between two young darting prospects in Group H.

articles.summary: Jutta Leerdam posted a full-length mirror selfie on Instagram, and the room behind her took up most of the frame.
articles.body: Jutta Leerdam posted a full-length mirror selfie on Instagram, and the room behind her took up most of the frame. The Dutch speed skater, who is engaged to Jake Paul, stood in front of white floating shelves stacked with high heels in black, nude and pink, with handbags on the rows above. A plain short message runs across the top of the mirror. The post comes about two months after Leerdam announced on YouTube that skating is off the schedule this season, and the closet shot gives followers a glimpse of time away from racing.What did Jutta Leerdam share in her new closet mirror selfie?Jutta Leerdam posted the shot as an Instagram Story on her official account. The Olympic champion holds a phone up to a large arched mirror that stands on its own, with silver open-toe heels in view. Floating shelves packed with dozens of pairs run along the left side, and the handbags are stored on the shelves above. The only text on screen is the “Xoxo” near the top of the mirror.The post arrives during a planned break. In a September YouTube video, Leerdam said: “I will not be competing this year, that’s for sure.” The announcement came seven months after the Milan Cortina Games, where the 27-year-old won the 1,000 meters in an Olympic record 1:12.31 and added silver in the 500. A 1,000-meter silver from Beijing in 2022 gives Leerdam three Olympic medals, and six adult world titles sit alongside them.The break keeps Leerdam out of next February’s world championships in Beijing. Even so, the Dutch star did not rule out a comeback, saying life and feelings can change at 27, so a full retirement did not feel right. Whether Leerdam is back in time for the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps is not known.In the same vlog, Leerdam called skating an “obsession” and described herself as multifaceted. A wall of heels and handbags is a small, personal look at life outside the rink, though Leerdam did not link the post to those comments.What the closet space looks likeThe room looks like a walk-in closet or dressing area. Glass doors, cabinets, cardboard boxes and clothing racks fill the background, and the space looks busy rather than staged. A beige handbag sits on the floor near the mirror, and sunlight falls across a light rug in front of it. The shelves still take up the left side of the frame, packed with heels. articles.title: NHL Trade Rumors: Could Sidney Crosby's continued support for Mike Babcock influence his future with Pittsburgh Penguins
articles.summary: Explore how Sidney Crosby's support for Mike Babcock may impact his future with the Pittsburgh Penguins amidst trade rumors and potential moves to the Edmonton Oilers.
articles.body: Sidney Crosby continues to be one of the most important players in Pittsburgh Penguins history, but his future continues to draw NHL attention and questions. His recent comments backing Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock have added another talking point to the discussions of a potential move.Crosby has spoken up for Babcock in the past, and his latest comments also shed light on their professional relationship. The comments don’t confirm any trade interest, but have sparked speculation as to whether Edmonton could become an option if Crosby eventually decides to leave Pittsburgh.Sidney Crosby's Mike Babcock praise draws Edmonton Oilers attentionHis steadfast backing of Mike Babcock has been noticed as the Edmonton Oilers are one of the clubs that could gain from adding an experienced center of Crosby’s stature.The reference report said Crosby recently praised the Oilers’ organization and direction under coach Babcock. He noticed that the players seemed to be on the same page and focused. His comments were an endorsement of the coaching atmosphere in Edmonton.Notably, Crosby’s latest assessment comes at a time when Babcock’s hiring in Edmonton has generated plenty of debate. The veteran coach has also coached Crosby on the international stage, giving the Penguins captain first-hand knowledge of his coaching methods.What makes Mike Babcock's coaching approach interesting to Crosby?Beyond their shared history with Team Canada, Crosby's appreciation for Babcock runs deeper. In September of 2026, the Pittsburgh captain phoned the coach to commend him for his organization, matchup management and communication of responsibilities to players.Crosby specifically took aim at Babcock’s bench management and his ability to establish a clear playing structure, The Hockey Writers and OilersNation reported.Could Pittsburgh Penguins' rebuilding plans influence Crosby's decision?It’s likely that Crosby’s contract status will be more relevant than his relationship with Babcock. The 39-year-old center is playing the final season of a two-year, $17.4 million deal that averages $8.7 million per year.But a departure is by no means certain. Crosby and his agent, Pat Brisson, have been discussing a possible extension with Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas, NHL.com reported. Crosby has also said he wants to keep playing for years to come.How Pittsburgh’s 2026-27 NHL season goes could play into those discussions. If the team chooses a longer-term roster transition, Crosby may eventually have to decide if another club offers a better chance to contend for another championship.Why could Edmonton Oilers become a potential destination?The Edmonton Oilers would be a team to watch if Crosby ever looked at options outside of Pittsburgh. The opportunity to play with Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl would give the veteran center a chance to play with two of the NHL's top offensive stars.Edmonton also may be an attractive option because of his familiarity with Babcock. But the Oilers will have to juggle their salary-cap situation, roster needs and the financial terms of a potential deal.There is no confirmation that Crosby wants to leave the Pittsburgh Penguins or that Edmonton has begun trade talks. His praise of Babcock should be seen as professional respect, not a harbinger of a future move.If Crosby ever thinks about switching, the 2027 offseason could be a significant point in his career, and meanwhile, an extension in Pittsburgh is a real possibility, and Edmonton is a speculative destination, not a known trade candidate.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NHL trade rumor: Why the Minnesota Wild could keep Quinn Hughes beyond the 2027 deadline despite contract uncertainty
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild are set to retain Quinn Hughes beyond the 2027 NHL trade deadline, prioritizing their Stanley Cup ambitions while navigating contract uncertainty. Discover the implications of this decision.

The strategy would give the Wild a chance to chase a deeper Stanley Cup playoff run with one of the league’s most influential defenders in the fold.Why are the Minnesota Wild reluctant to trade Quinn Hughes?There are several reasons why Minnesota might have preferred to keep Hughes:Stanley Cup aspirations: The Wild want to do what's best to give themselves a chance to compete for the championship, and not weaken their roster as they head into the playoffs.Defensive contribution: Hughes gives offensive production and puck movement and playmaking that’s hard to replace.Competitive position: Minnesota has played so well that keeping key players is more attractive than accumulating future draft picks.Playoff rental strategy: The franchise might be willing to let Hughes walk in free agency to better its chances of winning a championship right now.What is Quinn Hughes' contract situation in Minnesota?Quinn Hughes is entering the last year of his contract, and that brings questions about his long-term future with the Minnesota Wild.Formal extension talks are not reported to be taking place. But general manager Bill Guerin has taken a patient approach to the situation and has not shown any urgency to deal with the defenseman.Hughes’ performances just add to Minnesota’s reasons to keep him around. The defenseman has apparently scored 17 points, including five goals, during a brilliant 11-game point streak.His offensive production and impact from the blue line are a key part of the Wild’s competitive plans.Could Quinn Hughes join his brothers in New Jersey?The New Jersey Devils have been mentioned in NHL trade speculation involving Hughes because his brothers, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes, are on the team.Any possible reunion will always be a topic of discussion, but there is no indication that Minnesota is looking to move Quinn to New Jersey.The reported desire of the Wild to keep him around for the time being suggests that a family reunion isn't necessarily the catalyst for the trade chatter right now.How could keeping Quinn Hughes affect Minnesota Wild?The issue is that keeping Quinn Hughes could help Minnesota make a deep postseason run, but also poses a huge long-term contract risk.If the defenseman is unsigned at the end of the season, the Wild could lose him in free agency and get nothing in return via trade.But trading an elite defenseman while trying to win a Stanley Cup might be just as costly. Hughes gives you offensive creativity, defensive mobility and experience that would be especially valuable in the playoffs.The reported move suggests Minnesota is prioritizing its immediate championship hopes over potential future asset returns. articles.title: Braves Must Bring Back Raisel Iglesias
articles.summary: The Braves have the chance to re-sign Raisel Iglesias. With a 2.55 ERA and 34 saves last season, he is the missing piece for a championship run.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves have a clear path to a stronger bullpen, and the name on the shortlist is Raisel Iglesias. Even after adding Evan Phillips, the front office still has room to make a move that matters. MLB reporter Francys Romero states that the Braves are keen on extending their partnership with the veteran right-hander. The team is making a targeted effort to secure a proven closer.

Iglesias brings a track record that fits the team's needs perfectly. He finished the 2026 season with a 2.55 ERA and 34 saves, a career-high mark he has now reached four times. Battery Power notes that his consistency makes him a top name on the relief market. The 36-year-old posted a 61 ERA- and a 3.17 FIP across 59 appearances.

Braves fans know what Iglesias looks like in a clutch moment. He was reliable for the most part during his time in Atlanta. While he might not be the most dominant pitcher on the mound, he gets the job done. The Tigers are also interested, which drives up the price, but the Braves know his value best. His 1.1 fWAR would have made him the top reliever for Detroit by a wide margin.

Bringing him back avoids the risk of signing an unknown. The team already has the system in place for him to succeed. As Battery Power points out, his stats are in line with his four full seasons in Atlanta. It is easy to see him performing at that same level if he returns.

Other teams are circling, but the Braves have the edge on familiarity. Detroit sees him as a way to fix their own bullpen issues. However, Iglesias has already proven he can thrive in the pressure of Truist Park. The competition for his services is real, but the fit with Atlanta is obvious. He knows the staff, the fans, and the expectations.

The front office must act fast to beat out the Tigers. A deal could be simple if both sides agree on the value. The team has shown it is willing to spend to fortify the bullpen, as seen with the Phillips signing.

According to reports, the interest from multiple teams, including the Braves and Detroit Tigers, confirms his status as a top target. The Braves have the chance to keep a key player in the fold.

articles.title: Spurs Win Streak To 12, But Jazz Drop 12th Loss In A Row
articles.summary: The Spurs just won their 12th game straight while the Jazz lost their 12th. See how Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle changed the game.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs kept their hot hand going on Sunday night, beating the Utah Jazz 110-102 in Salt Lake City. This win marks the team's 12th straight victory, a streak that has fans buzzing across the league. Meanwhile, the Jazz are stuck in a deep hole, having lost 12 games in a row. It was a tough night for Utah, but San Antonio showed they are a team to watch right now. The Spurs struggled to put Utah away, but Dylan Harper delivered when the game was on the line. His late three-pointers helped San Antonio regain control and finish the comeback.

Dylan Harper led the charge with 31 points, 18 in the 4th quarter, and nine rebounds, proving he can carry a team when needed. He tied the game at 100 with back-to-back three-pointers when the clock was winding down. Then Stephon Castle hit two free throws to put the Spurs ahead 102-100 with 2:30 left. Castle finished with 20 points and nine assists, showing he is a key part of this winning formula. The Spurs outscored the Jazz 27-5 in fast-break points, which really opened up the floor for them. Victor Wembanyama also played a huge role, finishing with 26 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks. His presence in the paint forced the Jazz to make mistakes they couldn't recover from.

The Jazz tried to keep it close, with Mo Bamba leading Utah with 26 points and shooting a perfect 6-for-6 from three-point range. Darryn Peterson added 17 points, and Keyonte George had 13 points and eight assists. But San Antonio just wouldn't let them get comfortable. Even though Utah scored seven baskets over eight possessions late in the first quarter to take a 33-23 lead, the Spurs answered back quickly. A 10-0 run in the third quarter put them up 79-70, giving them a cushion heading into the 4th. The Spurs' ability to run the floor and score in transition made all the difference in the showdown.

Winning 12 games in a row is no small feat, especially in a league as tough as the NBA. This streak shows that the Spurs have found a rhythm that other teams will struggle to break. The Jazz, on the other hand, are facing a crisis of confidence after their 12th straight loss. They had a chance to stay in the game, but a late run by San Antonio sealed the deal. Castle's steal and dunk with 47.2 seconds left capped a 14-4 run that extended the lead to 108-102. That final push showed the Spurs have the heart to close out tight games. Keldon Johnson chipped in 11 points and 10 boards, doing the dirty work that wins championships.

The Jazz will need to find a way to stop these runs if they want to turn their season around. San Antonio's defense was sharp, and their offense was clicking on all cylinders. The team's depth showed up again, with Luke Kornet getting an alley-oop dunk off an assist from Johnson. This kind of ball movement is what keeps a winning streak alive. As the season goes on, this 12-game streak will likely be the story everyone talks about in San Antonio. The Jazz have a long road ahead, but the Spurs are just getting started on their own. The final score of 110-102 was a clear sign of who is in charge right now.

articles.body:
With the Michigan football team's disastrous 31-7 loss to the Oregon Ducks last Saturday, it marks the fifth defeat in the last seven games for the program after starting the season 3-0. After Michigan football's beatdown at the hands of Oregon , head coach Kyle Whittingham would send a message to the fans about the season and the future of the program.

Speaking to the media on Monday, Whittingham was asked a myriad of questions, but one was his message to the Wolverines' fans about the direction of the team. He started by saying that the program had "no opportunity to recruit a class this year," and that the focus is to "stay the course."

"We inherited the team, which I'm not complaining about the team, but if there was deficiencies, we didn't have a chance to fill any of those needs through our own recruiting," Whittingham said, via 247 Sports. "So that would be nice to have a recruiting cycle to help bolster the roster and get any lack of depth or whatever we need addressed."

"It's a process. Sometimes things happen overnight," Whittingham continued. "Once in a while, you'll catch lightning in a bottle. There's been some teams that have turned things around just like that. Typically, those guys were hired in late November, early December, when we had a chance to recruit and get your roster."

Kyle Whittingham continues on Michigan football's disappointment

With the Michigan football team at 5-5, the goal now is to be bowl eligible, but the final remaining two games have the unranked team going up against undefeated No. 4 UCLA and then No. 20 Ohio State. Whittingham admitted that his sentiments 'sound like excuses,' but expressed that the blame is on him for the disappointment this season.

"So it's just a matter of if we wanted to stabilize a program that was in a little bit of disarray and win a championship and all that in the same year, that's a pretty tough order to accomplish all that," Whittingham said.

articles.title: Keelon Russell, Austin Mack and the 'only drama' for Alabama football vs. Vanderbilt
articles.summary: Here's what Ryan Grubb said about Keelon Russell, Austin Mack and the QB situation during Alabama vs. Vanderbilt.
articles.body:
Ryan Grubb was frustrated by Alabama football's performance against Vanderbilt.

He sped through the good things, admitting "there wasn't a ton" before he honed in on the competitive stamina, the disappointing drop of production after LSU and the product after a lackluster week of preparation. But before Grubb talked generally, he addressed Alabama 's quarterback situation.

"From our standpoint, it was not a question of whether Austin (Mack) could do it," Grubb said. "It's more about our commitment to Keelon (Russell)."

After Russell battled through an ankle injury and led Alabama to a road win against LSU, Russell's status remained in jeopardy as kickoff neared against Vanderbilt. Mack was expected to start, a reality Grubb said he made clear to Mack the night before, giving the caveat that Russell would play "if he's ready."

As Alabama went through warm ups, Russell did every drill with ease, excelled in the rollout work and "looked awesome," per Grubb.

"He's our starter, and we stay committed to that," Grubb said, seeing someone with the determination to get on the field and play.

Russell completed 22 of 33 pass attempts for 217 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. Mack was on the field during Alabama's victory formation.

"Handled like a champ," was how Grubb described Mack's reaction, and added that his backup QB was prepared to play, calling him "the pro, such a strong-minded kid."

"I think the only drama that there was was it was hard on Austin," Grubb said. "I think for any player to prep like Austin did, and for Keelon to step out there, but he understands our commitment. If it was flipped, he would want the same commitment to him as a starter. And so, again, I can't reiterate that enough, it really has nothing to do with Austin and everything to do with Keelon's our starter. We're committed to him."

articles.title: Eagles sign Zach Ertz to the 53-man roster ahead of Week 11 vs. Steelers
articles.summary: The Eagles signed Zach Ertz and John Ojukwu to the active roster, opened Will Shipley’s practice window and announced practice-squad moves
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles began their return from the bye with additions to the active roster and a step toward getting another running back available.

Philadelphia announced Monday that it signed tight end Zach Ertz and offensive tackle John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for running back Will Shipley. The Eagles also signed running back Jaydon Blue, linebacker Chance Campbell and tight end Hayden Rucci to the practice squad, releasing defensive back Shaun Wade.

The moves come as Philadelphia prepares to host Pittsburgh on Sunday, looking to end a seven-game losing streak.

Zach Ertz, John Ojukwu join Eagles' active roster

Ertz and Ojukwu move into active-roster roles after previously spending time on Philadelphia's practice squad. Both were elevated for the Eagles' October game against Jacksonville in London. Ertz gives Philadelphia another experienced option alongside Dallas Goedert, Grant Calcaterra and rookie Eli Stowers. The veteran returned to the organization in September and has three receptions for 22 yards this season.

His signing allows the Eagles to carry him on the active roster rather than rely on a standard practice-squad elevation to make him available for a game. It does not guarantee a particular snap count or game-day role.

Ojukwu adds tackle depth after Philadelphia waived Fred Johnson on Friday. With Jordan Mailata and rookie Markel Bell handling the starting tackle assignments, Ojukwu gives the Eagles another option as they evaluate their protection and reserve combinations.

Will Shipley takes a step toward returning

Opening Shipley's practice window allows him to resume practicing while remaining on injured reserve. Philadelphia must activate him before he can return to game action; Monday's announcement does not establish that he will play against Pittsburgh. Shipley went on injured reserve Oct. 16. His potential return would give the Eagles another backfield option after injuries disrupted the rotation during the first half of the season.

Jaydon Blue returns to Eagles' practice squad

Blue rejoins the organization after Philadelphia waived him last week. His return preserves another running back option while the Eagles evaluate Shipley's progress. Campbell also returns to the practice squad, while Rucci joins the tight end group. Wade's release completes the changes to the developmental unit. The immediate additions are Ertz and Ojukwu. Shipley's availability remains a separate decision as Philadelphia begins the final eight games of its season.

articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 11: Latest news, updates for Drake Maye, Kenneth Walker III, Brock Bowers, more players for fantasy football
articles.summary: We go over the Week 11 NFL Injury Report with latest news and updates, plus fantasy football analysis for key players.
articles.body:
It was a rough week for the New England Patriots over in Germany. As we look over the Week 11 NFL injury report, the Patriots are going to pop up quite a bit going into their bye. We also have five other teams on bye — the Packers, Seahawks, Browns, Falcons and Rams. Those teams will hopefully get healthier over that span.

Below, we'll go over the latest injury news, providing updates on key players for fantasy football.

Drake Maye, NE (ankle) — Out indefinitely

Baker Mayfield, TB (lower leg) — Could miss Week 11

Maye : New England heads into its bye, though the season may be lost coming out of it. At this point, it's feared Maye has a fractured ankle and could need season-ending surgery. At the very least, he could miss multiple games or be placed on IR. It's almost helpful that New England is on bye in Week 11, as fantasy managers would already be looking for a Maye replacement or streaming option.

If Maye is done for the season, it's difficult to trust anyone on this offense. There are injuries and ailments everywhere, from A.J. Brown to Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The Pats are well behind the 8-1 Bills in the AFC East, though are still in the wild-card picture. But if Maye is out, that outlook could change fast. If you have any skill position player on New England, be sure to have contingency plans. This team could turn into a fantasy wasteland soon.

Mayfield : The Bucs are coming out of the Week 10 bye but may be without Mayfield . He suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9's loss to Chicago, and the extra rest didn't appear to help. If Mayfield is out against Detroit in Week 11, Jalon Daniels, who started three games earlier in the season, would get another shot. With so many teams on bye and Maye managers searching for answers, Daniels isn't a bad waiver add. Tampa Bay has a pretty soft schedule the rest of the season. Expect the Bucs to continue to ride the running game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.

Walker : The Chiefs added Walker to the injury report last Friday and he was swiftly ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. As a result, rookie Emmett Johnson thrived in lead-back duties, totaling 171 yards on 28 touches (six catches) with two TDs for 32.1 fantasy points. Reports suggest this will be a short absence for Walker and he should be back Week 11 against the Cardinals.

If Walker is back, he should return to his role as the lead back and get the majority of the work. Johnson has played well enough to warrant touches, however, and could get extra work given the opponent. Kansas City is heavy favorites in Week 11, and if the team pulls away, we could see Walker rest and Johnson get work in garbage time. If Walker is active, you're playing him, of course. But if you were able to snag Johnson off the wire, he's also in play as a flex option.

Texans RBs : Marks was forced to leave Week 10 against the Browns due to a concussion. He's unlikely to go Thursday against the Colts. Head coach DeMeco Ryans also doesn't know if Montgomery will be ready on the short week. If both backs are out, it's looking like Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will split the work out of the backfield.

While it's a good matchup, if both Marks and Monty are out, neither depth back is a strong fantasy play. Each would be a risky flex option. Instead, expect the Texans to lean on the passing game, which has looked good over the past four games. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte remain interesting adds off the waiver wire depending on league size/format.

Burden : The Bears were on bye in Week 10 and Burden has had ample time to get right. We'll see what his practice status looks like but he'll need to clear protocol in order to play this week against the Saints. If Burden misses the game, it's a bump up for Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland in the pass game, while we may see more targets for Kalif Raymond.

Evans : The Niners may not be in a rush to get Evans back given the 46 points the offense scored on Sunday against the Cowboys. The veteran wideout missed his third straight game but will have a shot at returning in Week 11 against the Vikings, not an ideal spot. San Francisco also has a pretty crowded receiving room with Deebo Samuel Sr. returning and Keenan Allen coming over via trade, not to mention George Kittle and the emerging Jordan Watkins. If Evans can get back in Week 11, he's a low-upside WR2/3 given the matchup.

Bowers : Reports came out that Bowers avoided a major injury in Week 10's loss to the Seahawks, which is good news. He's considered day-to-day and has a shot to play in Week 11 against the Broncos. The tight end didn't get much time to develop chemistry with new starting QB Fernando Mendoza on Sunday, catching just two passes for 18 yards before exiting. With Mendoza under center, it's a slight downgrade for Bowers, but he's still a locked-in TE1. If Bowers ends up missing the game, Michael Mayer isn't a bad streaming option. articles.title: Five-try Joseph set to start against All Blacks
articles.summary: England's Will Joseph is in line to retain his place for Saturday's blockbuster Nations Championship meeting with New Zealand after scoring five tries agains...
articles.body:
England's Will Joseph is in line to retain his place for Saturday's blockbuster Nations Championship meeting with New Zealand after scoring five tries against Japan.

In the absence of the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Joseph is understood to be in pole position to reprise his role on the wing after a performance packed with pace and finishing ability.

Joseph scored a hat-trick inside the first 19 minutes, on the way to becoming only the fifth England men's player to score five tries in one match.

He also headed the team's charts for metres carried (224) and top speed (21.7mph).

The 24-year-old won his second Test cap in Saturday's 78-15 thrashing of the Brave Blossoms, four and half years after making his debut as a teenager.

After a late cameo as a replacement in England's second Test win over Australia in July 2022, Joseph struggled to fulfil his promise. Boyhood club London Irish went into liquidation and a stint at Harlequins was hampered by injury and a lack of game time.

However, Joseph has been a key part of Gloucester's resurgence this season and, watched by elder brother and former England centre Jonathan Joseph, he made a sensational return to international rugby at Allianz Stadium last weekend.

"He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live of Joseph's ability.

"He floats, doesn't he?" added England team-mate Ben Earl to BBC Sport.

"The way he carries himself, he does really move like his brother. They are so, so similar."

With Feyi-Waboso ruled out of the autumn by an ankle injury, Cadan Murley is the other specialist wing in England's squad vying with Joseph for a spot alongside likely first-choice Tommy Freeman in the back three.

After victories over Australia and Japan this autumn, England are second in the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings and in line for a play-off meeting with South Africa on finals weekend on 27-29 November.

However, that could change considerably, with New Zealand leading the southern hemisphere table and second-place South Africa taking on Ireland, who are behind England only on points difference.

articles.title: Week 11 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups: Kaelon Black among top adds with 6 teams on bye, injuries piling up
articles.summary: Boone goes over his top waiver wire adds at each position going into Week 11 of the fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

The Titans are pushing the pace on offense and are using a no-huddle approach at one of the highest rates in the league. That's helped Ward to his two best fantasy results of the season in the last two games, finishing as the QB4 in Week 8 and coming off the bye he's sitting as the QB12 with only Monday Night Football left to be played.

Ward has also done this without his top receiver Carnell Tate, who's missed the last two outings but is expected to return for their Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys. It's the right time to get back since Tennessee is third in neutral pace of play and Dallas leads the league in that category — setting up a massive opportunity for fantasy scoring.

It's also worth noting that Ward has one of the five easiest fantasy schedules for QBs the rest of the way, including matchups with the Commanders (Week 13), Lions (Week 14), Colts (Week 15) and Raiders (Week 16). Though I'm still only valuing Ward as a fantasy QB2 streamer, don't be surprised if we see the former first-round pick finish hot down the stretch.

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

Black has been one of the stars of this column all season long and the fact that he's still available in over 60% of fantasy leagues is a massive mistake by managers.

Just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson last week, when Kenneth Walker III got hurt in practice. The Chiefs' rookie stepped into the starting role and delivered 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. That's the kind of upside Black offers if Christian McCaffrey were ever to miss time.

Even with CMC active, Black's role has grown in recent weeks resulting in 59 yards and TD in Week 7, a bye in Week 8, 70 yards in Week 9 and 68 yards and a TD last week. Most importantly, he's been given at least 11 touches in each of those games. When you're playing in one of the best offenses in the NFL, that kind of volume makes you a strong RB3/flex option with weekly RB2 upside when you find the end zone.

Don't let Black remain on the waiver wire any longer, he should be rostered in 100% of leagues.

Baker Mayfield is banged up and might sit out this week, which would put Jalon Daniels back under center. The rookie performed well in his three starts earlier in the season, but be prepared for the Bucs offense to lean even heavier on the run.

Gainwell has displayed weekly RB3/flex value over the last three games with 88 yards in Week 7, 140 yards in Week 8 and 76 yards in Week 9 before the team went on bye.

Bucky Irving is the unquestioned starter in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell needs to be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if injuries strike.

Even after a potential Jonathan Taylor trade failed to materialize, the Colts continued to split RB volume with the veteran turning his 18 touches into 103 scrimmage yards and McGowan chipping in with 77 yards and a TD on 12 opportunities.

It's the second consecutive game where the rookie reached the end zone, making him a legitimate RB3/flex option in fantasy, even as Taylor's running mate.

We could also see the team shut Taylor down at some point in the final two months, if he gets even the slightest injury. There's no reason to risk your star on a team that's going nowhere. If that occurs, McGowan would be a fantasy RB2 in whatever games he starts.

Woody Marks suffered a concussion and is unlikely to be cleared before Thursday's game against the Colts. David Montgomery, who hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury, returned to practice last week and put in a full session on Friday, but was ultimately ruled out for the game. That puts Montgomery on track to potentially play against the Colts, unless he suffered a setback.

If Montgomery can't go, then Demercado would be the next man up. He's earned 15 touches while playing behind Marks the last two games, only managing 39 scoreless scrimmage yards. In that scenario, Demercado would be a volume-based fantasy RB3.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt is 52% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add, if available.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at NYG (37% rostered)

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared coming off Denver's Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens get all the headlines, Flournoy has become a very consistent contributor in the Cowboys' passing attack.

The 27-year-old has at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in six straight games, finishing as a top-24 fantasy WR in five of those outings.

Even as the third pass-catcher in Dallas, Flournoy can be started in fantasy as a WR3/flex option, especially in an uptempo contest against a Titans defense allowing the most points to wideouts.

Despite not earning the kind of volume we'd like to see from a full-time receiver, Williams has been productive most weeks. The rookie has at least 50 yards or a touchdown in three of his last four games since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season.

Until he sees more consistent targets, it's hard to trust Williams as anything more than a flex option. However, his schedule is favorable in the coming weeks with the Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. With Stefon Diggs drawing the attention of top corners, Williams could earn more volume during that span.

Mitchell's outlook is complicated. Omar Cooper Jr. is dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him for a few games. That would condense the crowded receiver room down to Mitchell and Garrett Wilson, making Mitchell a possible WR3/flex option in fantasy.

Unfortunately, Geno Smith also suffered an ankle injury that might sideline him. Rookie backup Cade Klubnik represents a significant downgrade that would lower the ceiling of all the skill positions players in New York's offense.

So, Mitchell is a tentative add who could be started if Cooper misses time and if Smith doesn't. The fact that I'm writing about him in the waiver wire column is a clear sign we've reached Week 11 and the pickups are getting thin.

Jordyn Tyson is 58% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Keenan Allen is 59% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Tyson, if available.

Tank Dell is 51% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Tyson, Allen, Flournoy, Williams and Mitchell, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 59% rostered but would be the No. 7 WR add behind Tyson, Allen, Flournoy, Williams, Mitchell and Dell, if available.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Brock Bowers hurt his ankle on Sunday, but thankfully the team believes he avoided a major injury and should return "sooner rather than later."

Whether that means he'll be ready for their Week 11 date with the Broncos, remains to be seen.

Denver is one of the five easiest matchups for fantasy tight ends, so Mayer would immediately be in the streamer mix if he's called upon to start.

Since McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has averaged the ninth-most targets among tight ends and turned in three games with over 50 yards in five outings.

Okonkwo was well on his way to a much bigger day this past week, but his ongoing back injury caused him to miss part of the contest. With Okonkwo not playing his usual snaps, backup Ben Sinnott turned in four catches, 42 yards and a touchdown.

As long as he stays healthy, Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Aside from taking advantage of the Cowboys defense in Week 8, Allgeier has struggled to make his mark with Jeremiyah Love on IR. Allgeier only managed 46 yards on 19 touches in Week 9 and turned his five carries into 14 yards on Sunday. With so many injuries to the Cardinals offense, Allgeier isn't likely to provide much value moving forward.

The Patriots have lost Drake Maye for an extended stretch and possibly the rest of the season . That's why you see so many Pats in the drop section, including Brown (who's hurt as well), Douglas, Henderson, Kiner and Henry. There's very little value in New England with Tommy DeVito slated to start when they return from their Week 11 bye.

Since his back to back 80-yard games a month ago, Bernard has failed to top 30 yards in any of his past three outings. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson eventually returning, Bernard can be dropped in favor of a pickup who offers more upside.

articles.title: Gorka Abascal, joya del Real Madrid, se pierde el Mundial Sub-17 con la Selección Colombia
articles.standfirst: Gorka Abascal es baja confirmada para el Mundial por lesión
articles.summary: Gorka Abascal es baja confirmada para el Mundial por lesión
articles.body: A pocos días de su debut en la gran cita orbital, la Selección Colombia Masculina Sub-17 recibió una noticia que sacudió los planes del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Fredy Hurtado. El mediocampista Gorka Abascal, una de las grandes promesas formadas en la cantera del Real Madrid, sufrió una lesión de última hora en su último compromiso con el conjunto español y quedó oficialmente descartado para disputar la Copa Mundial Sub-17 de la FIFA Catar 2026. De acuerdo con el comunicado oficial emitido por la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol, Abascal padece una lesión muscular de grado II en el oblicuo interno derecho. Esta afección corresponde a una rotura parcial de las fibras de uno de los músculos abdominales esenciales para la estabilidad y la rotación del tronco. Los especialistas señalan que este tipo de dolencias requiere un periodo de recuperación estimado entre tres y seis semanas de baja absoluta, lo que imposibilita por completo su participación en el certamen que se llevará a cabo en territorio catarí del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre. Nacido en Bilbao (España) el 1 de octubre de 2010, Gorka Abascal posee una doble nacionalidad gracias a sus raíces: es hijo de padre español y madre colombiana. Su talento precoz lo llevó a destacar desde muy joven en el fútbol formativo del Athletic Club, para posteriormente dar el salto en 2025 a las divisiones inferiores del Real Madrid, donde actualmente milita en el Juvenil B. Aunque no pudo estar presente en el Sudamericano Sub-17 donde la 'Tricolor' se coronó campeona en Paraguay, Abascal se había ganado la confianza del estratega Fredy Hurtado tras destacadas actuaciones en partidos amistosos y en la UEFA Friendship Cup Sub-18. Su visión de juego, despliegue físico y potente pegada lo perfilaban como un bastión fundamental en el mediocampo del combinado nacional. Ante la baja irreparable del juvenil del Real Madrid, el cuerpo técnico nacional no tardó en mover ficha. El jugador elegido para ocupar su lugar en la lista definitiva de 21 convocados es Juan José Palacio, mediocampista perteneciente al Envigado Fútbol Club. Palacio ya venía trabajando de cerca con el grupo durante la concentración previa realizada en la ciudad de Barranquilla, lo que facilitará su integración inmediata a la delegación que emprende viaje rumbo a Doha para ultimar detalles de cara al debut.

articles.summary: Lo que debía ser una fiesta deportiva y un duelo definitivo por el ascenso en el fútbol profesional colombiano se convirtió en una auténtica batalla campal. Los incidentes ocurridos en el estadio Centenario de Armenia, en el marco del partido entre el Deportes Quindío y el Real Cartagena por los cuadrangulares del Torneo BetPlay, continúan generando ondas expansivas. En las últimas horas, nuevos videos han salido a la luz pública, revelando la magnitud de los ataques contra la fuerza pública, los destrozos en las tribunas y los momentos de pánico que se vivieron tanto al interior como en los alrededores del escenario deportivo.
articles.body: Lo que debía ser una fiesta deportiva y un duelo definitivo por el ascenso en el fútbol profesional colombiano se convirtió en una auténtica batalla campal. Los incidentes ocurridos en el estadio Centenario de Armenia, en el marco del partido entre el Deportes Quindío y el Real Cartagena por los cuadrangulares del Torneo BetPlay, continúan generando ondas expansivas. En las últimas horas, nuevos videos han salido a la luz pública, revelando la magnitud de los ataques contra la fuerza pública, los destrozos en las tribunas y los momentos de pánico que se vivieron tanto al interior como en los alrededores del escenario deportivo. El compromiso de la quinta fecha del grupo B era de alta tensión. El Deportes Quindío buscaba un resultado que lo acercara de manera definitiva a la gran final, pero enfrente tuvo a un ordenado Real Cartagena que supo golpear con anotación de Edison López y mantener la ventaja parcial. El punto de quiebre de la noche se dio en los minutos de reposición. Cuando el cronómetro marcaba el 90+5', el volante Jarlan Barrera marcó lo que parecía ser el 0-2 definitivo a favor de la visita. Este tanto desató la furia incontenible de un sector de la tribuna local. La frustración escaló rápidamente: decenas de hinchas decidieron vulnerar los anillos de seguridad, invadieron el terreno de juego y obligaron a detener las acciones. Los jugadores de ambos planteles y el cuerpo referencial tuvieron que huir despavoridos hacia la zona de camerinos para poner a salvo sus integridad. Paradójicamente, tras casi una hora de suspensión y la posterior intervención de las autoridades para retomar el control del campo, el VAR analizó la jugada del segundo gol cartagenero, determinando una falta previa por lo que la anotación fue anulada. Sin embargo, el daño ya estaba hecho y el ambiente en las gradas era irreversiblemente hostil. El partido concluyó con un 0-1 adverso para los 'cuyabros'. Con el paso de las horas, los registros audiovisuales compartidos en plataformas digitales y medios de comunicación han expuesto crudas escenas de lo ocurrido. Los nuevos videos muestran cómo los desmanes trascendieron la simple invasión de cancha: Agresiones directas a la fuerza pública: Se observa a grupos desadaptados lanzar objetos contundentes y piedras contra los uniformados del Esmad y la Policía Metropolitana, quienes intentaban contener el avance de la turba. Vandalismo a las afueras del estadio: La violencia se trasladó a las calles aledañas al Centenario, donde vehículos particulares sufrieron daños materiales considerables y se reportaron afectaciones a la infraestructura urbana y patrullas institucionales. Destrozos internos: Las graderías del escenario deportivo también sufrieron daños estructurales y mobiliarios debido a la arremetida de los violentos. Ante la gravedad de los hechos, las reacciones del rentado nacional no se hicieron esperar. La Dimayor emitió un enérgico y duro comunicado este lunes, rechazando categóricamente los actos vandálicos que manchan el balompié de ascenso. "Cada episodio de violencia aleja a las familias de los estadios, pone en riesgo la integridad de las personas y destruye el espectáculo que millones de colombianos disfrutan cada semana... Llegó el momento de pasar de las palabras a las acciones", señaló la entidad en su misiva oficial. Asimismo, las autoridades locales y los entes de seguridad anunciaron medidas urgentes, entre las que destaca la creación de un grupo especializado de Policía judicial enfocado en individualizar, judicializar y capturar a los responsables de liderar estos desmanes, vandalizar bienes públicos y agredir a los policías en el marco de un espectáculo deportivo.
