articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Gerwyn Price produces controversial 145 checkout en route to routine victory over Sebastian Bialecki
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price busts his score after hitting D20 - 10 over his required tally, but is given leg on account of having been given incorrect information by referee; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports up until the final on November 22
articles.body:
Price, the three-time champion in Wolverhampton, came through 5-2 against Poland's Bialecki to book his place in the knockout stage.

However, there was controversy during the final Group E match as Price hit a 145 finish when he had 135 remaining in the fourth leg of the match.

'The Iceman' needed 135 to hold his throw, and he thought he had taken it out.

After hitting T19 he asked referee Charlie Corstophine what he had left and was told 88.

With 88 in mind, Price incorrectly hit T16 and D20 to finish off the leg and was given the hold.

Of course, Price believed he had gone the correct route for what he needed and went on to set up a last 16 date with Ryan Searle.

"I didn't know until I just walked in [to the press conference]," said Price. "I hit the first treble and I asked what I'd got left and he said 88.

"So I went treble 16 double top and he said game shot."

The Welshman admitted he was glad he didn't know or it would've weighed on his mind.

He added: "I know. I swear to God, I didn't even know until I came back here. I'm glad I didn't know because it probably would have played on my mind."

6.4.6 Errors in arithmetic shall stand as detailed on the scoreboard unless corrected prior to the next throw of the player whose score is in error. Any error in the score can be corrected by the Referee at any time until Game Shot is called in that leg.

6.4.7 If the incorrect score resulted in a leg win the result will stand unless corrected prior to the start of the next leg.

Both players went into the contest with one win each after beating Joe Hunt, which made it a straight shoot-out with only the group winners reaching the knockout stage this year.

Price had opened his week with a 5-3 win over Hunt on Saturday, racing into a 4-0 lead before Hunt won three legs in a row. Bialecki needed a deciding leg to beat Hunt 5-4 on Sunday.

The new format has already seen Ross Smith, Jonny Clayton and Luke Woodhouse suffer shock exits and Price said: "I prefer the old one [format], obviously. I've had some good memories here. You can slip up once, but in this one you can't.

"As you can see, a couple of good boys have gone, and they probably thought they'd have a second chance. But once you lose a game, that's it; you're gone."

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Luke Littler lands triple-bull checkout, as Gerwyn Price benefits from maths error
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler make it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage after a rare counting error and a sensational triple-bull checkout in Wolverhampton.
articles.body:
Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler both made it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage on a night featuring a bizarre maths error and a sensational triple-bull checkout.

Littler suffered a 5-4 defeat by Dutchman Niels Zonneveld but claimed the three legs he required to progress from the group stage.

The 19-year-old, egged on by the crowd at the Aldersley venue in Wolverhampton, improbably landed three darts on the bullseye to produce a remarkable 150 checkout and level the match at 4-4, only to lose the deciding leg.

Price, meanwhile, claimed a 5-2 victory over Sebastian Bialecki - although he was the beneficiary of an unusual mathematical mistake.

The Welshman was 2-1 up against Poland's Bialecki and required 135 to win the fourth leg.

Price's first dart hit treble 19, leaving him with 78, but he asked referee Charlie Corstorphine what he had left to score and was incorrectly told 88.

In good faith, Price promptly threw treble 16 and then double 20 to win the leg, having scored 145 - which should have bust him.

"A rare scoring error was made by the referee in the fourth leg of the match between Gerwyn Price and Sebastian Bialecki," organisers the PDC told BBC Sport in a statement.

"Under Darts Regulation Authority (DRA) rule 6.4, as the error was not corrected before the next leg began, the leg score stands as announced."

Price said he was unaware of the miscalculation until it was flagged up to him before he walked into a post-match news conference.

"I hit the first treble and I asked 'what have I got left?' and he said 88, so I threw treble 16 and double top, then he said 'game shot'," said fourth seed Price.

"I'm glad I didn't know, because it probably would have played on my mind."

What do DRA rules say about Price error?

The DRA's rulebook is clear if there has been an error in scoring which, although rare in professional darts, can sometimes occur.

The following clauses are what the rulebook , external says about the mistake involving Price:

6.4.6 Errors in arithmetic shall stand as detailed on the scoreboard unless corrected prior to the next throw of the player whose score is in error. Any error in the score can be corrected by the referee at any time until game shot is called in that leg.

6.4.7 If the incorrect score resulted in a leg win the result will stand unless corrected prior to the start of the next leg.

6.4.8 If the incorrect score resulted in the winning of a match the result will be considered as final when both players and the referee have left the playing area believing the match to be successfully completed.

Now, Big Blue gets the spotlight. ELI MANNING FINALLY REVEALS WHY HE WRIGGLED HIS WAY OUT OF PLAYING FOR CHARGERS Are they going to retell stories we've all heard in the nearly two decades since the G-Men won that ring? Of course. Will it be sweet to revisit the night Eli Manning and company broke New England's team of destiny? Absolutely. For Giants fans, that 2007 squad remains unforgettable because of how ugly things started. New York opened 0-2 with head coach Tom Coughlin on the hot seat before rattling off 11 straight road wins, including playoff upsets in Tampa, Dallas, and minus-one-degree Green Bay. SUPER BOWL CHAMPION PLAXICO BURRESS COMPARES PLAYING FOR JETS TO HIS TIME IN PRISON: 'A F—KING LOSER' After trading haymakers with New England in a 38-35 Week 17 loss, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo unleashed his four-end NASCAR pass rush in the rematch: Super Bowl XLII. Michael Strahan, Justin Tuck, and Osi Umenyiora sacked Tom Brady five times, holding the historic offense to 14 points. Then came the legendary fourth quarter: Manning slipping out of three jerseys, David Tyree pinning the football to his helmet, and Plaxico Burress — playing on a torn ankle ligament — hauling in the winning score. TOM BRADY ADMITS TO MORE MOTIVATION AFTER DEFLATEGATE SUSPENSION, REVEALS WHAT HE DID WHILE AWAY FROM PATRIOTS Manning and Strahan lead the documentary's Giants lineup alongside Coughlin, Spagnuolo, Tuck, Shaun O'Hara, Antonio Pierce, Sam Madison, Burress, and Tyree, joined by Brady. Hearing Brady get honest about the toughest loss of his career adds real juice to the show. Still, watching Netflix celebrate one of the landmark games in NFL history highlights a total joke. DREW BREES GIVES HIS STANCE ON ELI MANNING'S PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME CANDIDACY AMID STRONG DEBATE Super Bowl XLII defined an era, and Manning owns two Super Bowl MVPs against the Belichick-Brady dynasty, yet the Pro Football Hall of Fame has passed him over twice. Make it make sense. Leaving the architect of football's biggest upset out of Canton is a Giant mistake. articles.title: Nolan Wells murder case: New York man faces extradition after allegedly questioning police about college football player's death
articles.summary: Christian Anthony Claudio, 25, is facing possible extradition from New York to Mississippi after an arrest that has raised difficult questions about the
articles.body: Christian Anthony Claudio, 25, is facing possible extradition from New York to Mississippi after an arrest that has raised difficult questions about the limits of public scrutiny in a high-profile death investigation. Claudio says he contacted Mississippi police seeking answers about the death of 18-year-old Nolan Xavier Wells. He denies making threats. However, authorities have not publicly disclosed the charge behind the warrant, leaving key details of the case unclear as he prepares for another court appearance.Christian Anthony Claudio's arrest raises questions about the undisclosed chargesClaudio was arrested in Otsego County, New York, on October 31 under a law that allows authorities to detain people wanted in another state. He remains at Otsego County Jail while extradition proceedings move forward.His next hearing is scheduled for November 16 at 1 p.m. in Otsego County Court before Judge Michael F. Getman. Court records identify the Otsego County District Attorney's Office as the prosecuting authority and list the county's Public Defender's Office as his legal representative.Yet the public docket offers little information about the allegations. It reportedly contains no incident or arrest details, and the Mississippi warrant and supporting documents have not been made publicly available.That gap has become central to the growing attention surrounding Claudio's case. In videos recorded from jail and shared on social media, he has described his arrest as a response to his attempts to seek information about Wells.He also expressed fear about his safety, saying, “I do not feel safe, and I want to be watched.”His account has not been independently verified. No public recording of the calls or official explanation from the Mississippi department involved has emerged in the material cited by Emerald Book. The exact nature of the alleged conduct therefore remains unknown.Nolan Wells case puts Mississippi extradition process under scrutinyWells disappeared on July 4, 2026, during a boat trip to Horn Island with friends. His body was recovered two days later. A Mississippi grand jury declined to bring criminal charges in September, reportedly finding the available evidence consistent with accidental drowning. However, both the state autopsy and an independent examination commissioned by Wells' family listed his cause of death as undetermined.The findings have continued to fuel questions from relatives, activists and members of the public.Claudio's case has now added another layer of concern. Under interstate extradition rules, a person can face proceedings in a state where an alleged offence was received or took effect, even if the person was elsewhere when the conduct occurred. Phone calls and online messages can fall within this framework, depending on the allegations.However, the public cannot determine whether that applies to Claudio without knowing the specific charge and evidence.His November 16 hearing could address extradition, bail or other procedural matters. Until Mississippi releases more details, the central question remains unanswered: what exactly is Claudio accused of doing?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: On the road to Survivor Series: War Games, WWE Raw stopped at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh, North Carolina, with a show headlined by The Usos vs. 946's Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana.
articles.body:
On the road to Survivor Series: War Games, WWE Raw stopped at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh, North Carolina, with a show headlined by The Usos vs. 946's Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana.

Which team won the War Games advantage, and what else did WWE have in store for fans two weeks before the annual November extravaganza?

Find out in this recap, including grades and analysis of all of the night's action and top moments.

War Games Advantage Match: The Usos vs. Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana

Women's Intercontinental Championship Match: Iyo Sky vs. Raquel Rodriguez (c)

Last Time in Action: Cody Rhodes defeated Randy Orton (Crown Jewel, November 7)

Cody Rhodes and CM Punk, now co-captains of Team USA, according to the latter, announced that LA Knight is the latest addition to the team to kick off Monday's show.

The announcement came after The Miz and Kit Wilson interrupted proceedings, with the former making his case as he recalled coming up with both Rhodes and Punk in WWE.

Despite Rhodes seeming to take exception to Punk stepping on his toes, he agreed that the Hollywood A-Lister would not be part of the Survivor Series lineup.

When Knight entered the arena to a thunderous ovation and joined his new teammates in the ring, he allowed Miz to earn a spot by beating him and taking his. The heel agreed, and a referee joined the fray as the show went to commercial break.

Rhodes and Punk showed some fun chemistry as co-captains who do not agree. While there is a lightness to it now, do not be surprised if this, and whatever unfolds at Survivor Series, ends up laying the foundation for the WrestleMania 43 main event between them.

Miz and Kit Wilson are criminally underutilized at this point. Love them or not, they are immensely entertaining and should play a greater role.

Last Time in Action: LA Knight lost to Roman Reigns (Money in the Bank, October 10); Miz and Kit Wilson defeated Fraxiom (Main Event, October 28)

Not even outside interference from Kit Wilson could cash The Miz's ticket to Survivor Series Monday night.

At one point, the lackey interfered in his mentor's match with LA Knight, sending the Megastar crashing into the ring post and earning the upper hand for the heel. Instead, Knight fought his way back into the match, overcame one more attempt at interference from the protege, and caught Miz with Blunt Force Trauma for the win.

After the match, Wilson talked trash and paid for it, courtesy of a GTS from Punk and a Cross Rhodes from the American Nightmare.

This was a fun match, with two perpetually over Superstars and a red-hot crowd in Raleigh fueling them on. It did not reinvent the wheel, nor did it have to. The right person went over and the result is a stacked Team USA to this point.

It is an indictment of the creative team that Knight had not been more actively involved on TV following his Money in the Bank loss, in an attempt to keep him prominently featured. This was a nice rebound.

Last Time in Action: John Cena lost to Gunther (Saturday Night's Main Event, December 13)

The John Cena Classic will be an epic night of amazing action in which the WWE Universe will have the chance to let its voice be heard, the event's namesake announced Monday on Raw.

From there, Cena announced the latest invitee: Liv Morgan.

The Women's World Champion was the latest recipient of Cena's motivational speech, in which he called her proof that the fans' reaction will always matter. A big embrace wrapped up the announcement, just in time for Becky Lynch to make her entrance and come face to face with her Survivor Series opponent.

The Man told Morgan that while she has made a career of making everyone better, the current champion has made everyone around her worse, citing Raquel Rodriguez's Intercontinental Championship reign and the fact that Roxanne Perez is not already a champion.

She challenged Morgan to a fight, but the heel tried a cheap shot, only to be caught in a Manhandle Slam attempt. She escaped and scurried to the floor for sanctuary.

Cena did a hell of a job of presenting Morgan as a babyface who overcame the odds, won over the audience, and earned her place at the top of WWE, which would have been great if she was not a heel.

With that said, Cena's personal touch to each of these in-ring invitations to the main roster Superstars has gone a long way in heightening their importance.

Lynch laid the foundation for Perez to eventually step out of the shadows and challenge Morgan, something everyone knows is coming but has yet to manifest itself. Think it's a coincidence? There's a reason WWE highlighted it on its X account.

Last Time in Action: Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch lost to Liv Morgan (Money in the Bank, October 10); Jacy Jayne lost to Charlotte Flair (SmackDown, November 13)

Stephanie Vaquer was on her way to victory in a highly competitive match against the reigning Women's United States Champion, Jacy Jayne, on Monday night when Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid got involved and ensured there would be no decisive winner.

The heels beat down La Primera and appeared poised to leave her lying when Bayley made the save. She ran through and over the villains, but the numbers game proved too much for the babyfaces to overcome.

Fatal Influence stood tall to close out the segment.

Vaquer defeated Jayne via disqualification

The commentary team missed the opportunity to add a little more meaning to this one by reminding the viewing audience that it was Jayne who ended Vaquer's dominance over the NXT women's division last year, when she won its top prize.

Vaquer has been bitten by the injury bug this year, but she did not skip a beat in this one, looking every bit as great as she always has.

The match was solid throughout, and even though things got a bit messy late and the finish hurt its overall quality, the work was still good, and each made the other look strong.

Women's Intercontinental Championship Match: Iyo Sky vs. Raquel Rodriguez

Last Time in Action: Iyo Sky and Becky Lynch defeated Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez (Raw, November 9)

Not long after telling Liv Morgan that she makes everyone around her worse, Becky Lynch came to the aid of Iyo Sky, preventing the Women's World Champion from having too great an impact on the outcome and fighting her to the backstage area.

That was just minutes after Roxanne Perez's interference backfired.

What was a grueling match between Sky and Rodriguez culminated with the challenger delivering a tornado DDT, then scaling the ropes and perfectly executing an Over the Moonsault.

Three seconds later, the Genius of the Sky was the winner and the new IC champion.

Is it really a surprise to anyone that the best match on the show to this point involved Sky? The new champion is one of the best wrestlers on the planet, so it should not be.

Rodriguez does not get nearly enough credit for being the workhorse for the Judgment Day and the Raw women's division that she has become. She was excellent here, hanging with an acclaimed wrestler and never looking out of place. It is time to give La Ruda her flowers.

Lynch and Morgan getting involved felt unnecessary and probably would have been better had we not gotten the in-ring promo earlier in the night.

articles.title: Rams offensive line woes get even worse with latest injured reserve shakeup
articles.summary: The tail end of the Rams’ season is set to be a brutal stretch for an injured Los Angeles offensive line. Both Rams starting and backup centers, Coleman Shel...
articles.body:
The tail end of the Rams' season is set to be a brutal stretch for an injured Los Angeles offensive line.

Both Rams starting and backup centers, Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon, left in the first half of Sunday's 34-6 victory against the Arizona Cardinals and will be absent for the near future.

On Monday, California Post senior sports reporter Michael Duarte reported that Shelton "suffered from a severe hamstring strain" and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks, while McMahon has been placed on the team's injured reserve due to a knee injury.

Due to the Rams holding one of the more crowded injured reserves in football, McMahon runs the risk of his season coming to an end.

The NFL allows teams to activate eight players from the IR during the season, and Los Angeles has already activated three players this season, while still waiting to activate Davante Adams, Puka Nacua, Jordan Whittington, and Terrance Ferguson — which means McMahon might be the odd man out.

Beaux Limmer was filling in as Los Angeles' backup left guard in place of Steve Avila. But once McMahon left, Limmer filled in at center.

The Rams scored 17 points in the second half, and were led by their rushing attack.

Running back Blake Corum, who finished Los Angeles' first offensive possession of the second half with a one-yard rushing touchdown, finished the day with 17 carries for 100 yards.

Ronnie Rivers provided the perfect punch to support Corum, finishing with 15 carries for 81 yards.

It remains unknown if the Rams will go back to Limmer under center or if they sign a free agent, but the Rams are about to endure a crucial part of their schedule.

Due to Los Angeles having to play on Thanksgiving Eve, the Rams are on a "shortened bye week" right now and will have to play a 6-4 Packers team that is expected to have Micah Parsons suited up.

After that, the Rams will play a Thursday night matchup against the Chiefs, then an 8-1 49ers powerhouse the following week.

Their schedule will end with them playing the Seahawks twice during their final three weeks.

articles.title: Ben Hammond, Amani Hansberry and Jaylen Curry lead Virginia Tech to 85-68 victory over Richmond
articles.summary: (AP) — Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry totaled 15 points apiece, and Jaylen Curry scored 14 to lead Virginia Tech to an 85-68 victory over Richmond on Monday...
articles.body:
BLACKSBURG, Va. (AP) — Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry totaled 15 points apiece, and Jaylen Curry scored 14 to lead Virginia Tech to an 85-68 victory over Richmond on Monday night.

Hammond shot 6 for 15 with two 3-pointers and seven assists for the Hokies (5-0). Hansberry made 4 of 8 shots, sinking a 3-pointer and all six of his free throws, while Curry made 4 of 11 shots and went 6 for 6 at the foul line.

Tyler Johnson added a double-double off the bench for Virginia Tech with 10 points and 11 rebounds.

Jamie Kaiser Jr. finished with 17 points and six rebounds to pace the Spiders (3-2). Dominick Stewart added 13 points, and Amon Dorries scored 11.

Curry had six points, and Virginia Tech never trailed in a game-opening 20-9 run.

Efrem Johnson made two straight 3-pointers to increase the Hokies' lead to 35-19, and the advantage grew to 20 before Collin Tanner made a layup in the final seconds to cut it to 41-23 at the break.

Kaiser hit a 3-pointer and scored five, and Derin Saran's three-point play finished off a 15-0 run to start the second half as Richmond closed within 41-37.

Miles Heide tipped in a miss to end the run, and Hammond scored seven in a 14-4 spurt that left the Hokies leading 55-41 with 13:22 remaining. The Spiders got no closer than eight from there.

Richmond plays Western Kentucky on Friday at the Greenbrier Tip-Off.

Virginia Tech plays Northwestern on Friday at the Charleston Classic.

articles.title: Latest injury update, status on MSU starting QB Alessio Milivojevic
articles.summary: Here's what we know about the injury status of Spartans starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic
articles.body:
It remains uncertain if we will see Michigan State football starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic again this season after suffering a shoulder injury last week.

The Spartans starting quarterback was knocked out of the game late in the first half against Washington this past weekend. The injury came when Milivojevic was running for a first down and was hit hard by the Huskies defender. He never returned to the game after the hit and was seen on the sidelines in street clothes.

On Monday, Michigan State head coach Pat Fitzgerald provided no update on his quarterback's injury status. According to Chris Solari of the Detroit Free Press, Fitzgerald stated there was no update on Milivojevic that he would provide at this time and that the first update on his status will come out on Wednesday as part of the Big Ten's mandated availability reports.

Milivojevic has been battling another undisclosed injury that kept him out against UCLA last month. He returned from that injury to lead Michigan State to the upset win over Michigan last week and then started against Washington before getting knocked out of the game.

Michigan State sits at 3-7 overall and now is unlikely to reach a bowl game for the fifth straight season. The Spartans are more than two touchdown underdogs against Oregon this week, and that will be an even harder challenge for the Spartans should Milivojevic not be able to go play.

articles.title: Cameron Boozer scores 29 and Grizzlies hand the Wizards an 8th straight loss, 136-120
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 points in a matchup with top draft pick AJ Dybantsa of Washington, and the Grizzlies...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 points in a matchup with top draft pick AJ Dybantsa of Washington, and the Grizzlies rallied from 12 points down to hand the Wizards their eighth straight loss, 136-120 on Monday night.

Playing without leading scorer Ty Jerome, who has a sore right hip, the Grizzlies trailed 69-57 in the closing seconds of the first half but took control by outscoring the Wizards 42-18 in the third quarter. Boozer, the No. 3 pick in the draft after a standout season at Duke, finished 7 of 13 on 3-pointers, including two 3s during a 10-0 run that tied the game at 73-all.

Zach Edey had 23 points and 10 rebounds for the Grizzlies, who have won four of five and improved to 7-0 on the road. Javon Small had 12 points and 12 assists.

Dybantsa matched his season high with 21 points.

Washington hasn't won since beating Orlando on Nov. 2 to move to 4-3, and the skid has raised questions about the future of coach Brian Keefe. After a multiyear rebuild, the Wizards hoped to contend this season with veterans Anthony Davis and Trae Young playing alongside Dybantsa.

Davis led the Wizards with 23 points. Young, held scoreless for the first time in his career in Sunday night's 147-119 loss to visiting Houston, had 13 points on 3-of-10 shooting and 12 assists.

Young had 10 assists by halftime, the first Wizards player to do that since Tyus Jones on March 10, 2024 at Miami. The only other player with 10 assists in a half this season was Atlanta's Jalen Johnson on Oct. 26 against Houston.

The Grizzlies, who entered the game fourth in the NBA in offensive rating, shot 55.8% from the field.

Grizzlies: At Cleveland on Wednesday night.

Top 2027 recruit Haylen Ayers has committed to Vanderbilt , Rivals has learned. The 6-1 guard from Jackson (TN) University School of Jackson chose the Commodores over UConn.

"It's a very strong relationship with them," she previously told Rivals. "I think it started early and it's just kind of built from there. I think being able to watch them this past season and seeing where I would fit in and the style of play is exactly where I can visualize myself being in the next four years. I also think that they're really good people there and it would be really cool to continue my mom's legacy."

There were several factors that played a role in her decision.

"I think it's going to be where I fit in," she said of deciding factors. "Just with the team, the incoming people that are going to be there when I'm there, and how well I fit in. I think one thing that would stand out to me is how well we communicate with each other. I'm really big on relationships, and I think that's something that is going to continue to elevate me as a player and a person as I go along this journey. I think that's something that's really going to be the top priority when I look at a school is the relationships that I have, not only with the coaches but the players, because off the court is just as important on the court."

Vanderbilt is getting an elite player in Ayers.

"I think my biggest strength is being unselfish," she said. "I'm willing to let others score instead of me. I'm willing to make the extra pass, I'm willing to go get a defensive stop."

articles.title: Donovan Mitchell’s 39 points help push Cavaliers past Bulls 126-115
articles.summary: The Cavaliers were able to resist any potential Bulls comeback.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers , coming off an exceptional win against the Dallas Mavericks with the reserves, had all fans wondering how the starters would respond. The win on Saturday was driven by intensity, effort, and a team that never let their foot off the gas.

The starters for Cleveland against the Bulls had a lesser opponent in front of them; however, the effort felt like an improvement from past games in the early season.

Right off the bat, the Cavaliers were honed in offensively by scoring through the paint; within the first few possessions, Jarrett Allen was rim running with little to no resistance.

Cleveland kept with this mindset and seemed to prioritize their effort on the glass and scoring inside. This proved to be the correct mindset. The Cavaliers scored scoring 68 of their 126 points around the cup. The Cavs were also outhustling the Bulls on the boards, 51-37.

Monday proved another great night for the young bucks in Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas. Proctor, who was the star of Saturday night's game, was given the nod with the starters in the absence of Evan Mobley. Proctor fit in seamlessly with the starters, scoring 17 points and finding his spots without hijacking the offense.

Thomas (9 points and 6 rebounds) likewise was able to find his spots and continues to impress. His knack for scoring from almost anywhere on the court allows him to fit with any five-man lineup the Cavaliers throw out.

At the end of the day, this game was won by Donovan Mitchell, who scored the game-high 39 points on 16-25 shooting. Whenever it felt like the Bulls would attempt to mount a rally, it was Mitchell who would offer his own counterpunch to end the counter.

Mitchell's ability to sense when his buckets were needed was nice to see from the leader of the team. The Bulls, at the end of the day, do not have someone of Mitchell's caliber who can respond to the nuclear levels of scoring that Donovan can.

While not the dominant effort some were hoping for, it is nice that the Cavaliers can win games like this without having to sweat it out until the final buzzer. It isn't the 30-point blowouts we saw a few years ago, but this feels like a step in the right direction.

The Cavaliers look to take this momentum into their next matchup on Wednesday against the Memphis Grizzlies.

articles.title: Victoria Police arrest a man over theft of Makybe Diva’s three Melbourne Cup trophies
articles.summary: Police have arrested a man but have not yet recovered the three Melbourne Cup trophies won by Makybe Diva that were stolen from a display cabinet at the Flem...
articles.body:
MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — Makybe Diva's three Melbourne Cup trophies are missing after a heist at Flemington Racecourse.

Victoria state police on Tuesday said officers raided a home in Mount Waverley, in the southeastern suburbs of Melbourne on Monday night as part of investigations into the burglary and arrested a 36-year-old man, who was later released pending summons to appear in court.

"It is alleged two men attended the racecourse ... and smashed a cabinet inside the venue at 6:30 a.m." Monday, Victoria Police said in a statement.

Makybe Diva won the Melbourne Cup in 2003, 2004, and 2005 and the trophies had been on public display since September at Flemington Racecourse, where the southern hemisphere's most prestigious horse race is held annually on the first Tuesday of November.

Police said the trophies stolen from the glass display case were each valued at 1 million Australian dollars ($675,000).

Makybe Diva, known widely in local racing circles as "the people's horse," died in February at the age of 26. She was the only horse to have won the Melbourne Cup three years in a row in a race which was first held in 1861.

"Hopefully we can get them back in one piece," former owner Tony Santic told Melbourne radio 3AW. "It's more than devastating. I just can't believe it. Hopefully we get them back in one piece."

The Victorian Racing Club said it was "devastated" by the theft and it was in contact with Santic.

articles.body: CM Punk and Bayley joined at a WWE live event in Detroit on Saturday, and AJ Lee had plenty to say about it. The pair beat The Vanity Project’s Jackson Drake and Myka Lockwood in a mixed tag team match on the NXT Holiday Live Tour. Afterward, they FaceTimed Lee while the crowd watched. Bayley then posted highlights on Instagram, and Lee answered in the comments. Lee’s verdict was short and left little doubt. The two are close friends away from the ring, but they have not shared the screen in WWE before.What did AJ Lee say about CM Punk and Bayley’s match?Bayley set the tone with her Instagram caption. “Please enjoy these 2 minutes of me and @cmpunk with those annoying, stuck up, conceited, but I guess pretty talented Vanity Project IDIOTS,” she posted. “Special appearance from our wife, @theajmendez #NXTDetroit.”Lee, who was tagged in the post, replied in the comments. “This is the hottest tag match of all time,” Lee wrote.Lee has a recent history with Punk in the ring. She returned to WWE last year to help him in his rivalry with Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch. The duo beat Rollins and Lynch in a mixed tag team match at Wrestlepalooza. At Survivor Series 2025, Lee made Lynch tap out to the Black Widow in the Women’s WarGames Match. Her last appearance on WWE programming came at this year’s Show of Shows. articles.title: Former Villanova Big To Miss Time Following Ankle Surgery
articles.summary: Duke Brennan had some nice moments for the Wildcats last season.
articles.body:
Former Villanova center and current Oklahoma Sooner Duke Brennan will miss significant time following ankle surgery.

Brennan suffered a right ankle injury on Sunday during practice. The team announced on Monday that he would undergo surgery.

Brennan started the first four games of the year for Oklahoma. He averaged 8.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game.

There are some players that leave a strong impression in a short amount of time. Brennan can be viewed as that with Villanova.

Brennan transferred in after two years at Grand Canyon. He played in and started 32 games for the Wildcats and averaged 12.4 points and 10.3 rebounds. The big man helped Villanova return to the NCAA Tournament after a three-year hiatus. He finished the year with 14 double-doubles.

There were many big performances from Brennan in a Villanova uniform. Here were some of his best from last season:

11/8 vs. Queens: 17 points, 20 rebounds, 7-for-14 FG

12/13 vs. Pitt: 24 points, 9 rebounds, 8-for-8 FG, 8-for-12 FT

1/24 at UConn: 16 points, 14 rebounds, 4-for-6 FG, 8-for-9 FT

2/14 at Creighton: 21 points, 12 rebounds, 8-for-9 FG

3/7 vs. Xavier: 20 points, 13 rebounds, 9-for-12 FG

Brennan was an impact transfer for the Wildcats who helped get the team back on the right track in year one under Kevin Willard. Hopefully is he able to return to the court soon.

articles.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks are not having the best start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Chicago has lost more games than they envisioned heading into mid-November. I...
articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks are not having the best start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Chicago has lost more games than they envisioned heading into mid-November. In fact, they've lost seven of their last eight games.

Chicago has a chance to get back on track on Tuesday. Connor Bedard will lead his team into battle against the Toronto Maple Leafs and Gavin McKenna , the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft. Before this game, Bedard told reporters that he has been quite impressed with McKenna this year.

"I think when you're in Toronto, you hear about everything a guy does, so it's even another level for him than it was for me … just being in that market and everything you do, if he turns a puck over or anything, which is crazy," Bedard said, via NHL.com. "He's done great and he's playing unreal. He's doing everything right, so it's fun to see."

McKenna and Bedard came into the NHL under similar circumstances. Bedard was the No. 1 pick in his draft back in 2023. He went straight to the NHL, as well, much like McKenna has now.

So far, McKenna has had an up-and-down rookie campaign. The Maple Leafs rookie has six goals and 13 points through his first 22 games in the league. However, there have been some mistakes that come with the territory of being a newcomer in the NHL.

Bedard and McKenna could be rivals for the foreseeable future in this league. We could see that rivalry begin in real time on Tuesday night. It will certainly be interesting to see which player can lead their team to victory.

articles.title: Malachi Moreno’s career night saves Kentucky Basketball from a sluggish first half vs. Grambling State
articles.summary: Malachi Moreno took over the second half with a career-high performance to secure the win.
articles.body:
Malachi Moreno's second-half performance is what Kentucky Basketball needs to see from him every night going forward. The Kentucky big man had a career night against Grambling State on Monday in a game Kentucky badly needed to show reasons for hope after last week, and he did just that.

The Wildcats also needed his second-half surge to overcome a sluggish finish to the first half and pull away for the victory. In the opening 20 minutes, it looked like the Wildcats had found a little momentum when Justin McBride nailed a three-pointer to push the lead to 19-8 with just over 12 minutes remaining.

But to Grambling State's credit, the Tigers battled hard for the rest of the half, weathering the early storm to head into the locker room trailing by just six points. That was only after a Mason Williams buzzer-beater.

The biggest test of the night was always going to come in the paint, though. Moreno knew he would have his hands full with Isaiah Miranda, Grambling's 7-foot star.

For the first half, that heavyweight bout was an even matchup. Miranda went into the break with seven points and four rebounds, while Moreno countered with eight points and four boards of his own.

Moreno came out of the locker room and established his dominance on the block. He anchored the paint, demanded the basketball, and finished the night with a career-high in points and rebounds.

22 points, 12 rebounds, 4 steals, and 3 blocks. Great stat line from Moreno tonight, even if you account for the competition. Over his last three games, he's averaging 18.3 points, 9.3 boards, 4.0 assists, 2.3 blocks, and 1.6 steals per game.

That is the kind of commanding performance I, and I am sure you, want to see from Moreno every single night. It should not matter who the opponent is. This is the kind of player Moreno has to be for this Kentucky team.

Seeing Moreno break through with a career-high scoring and rebounding performance while imposing his will on the glass is exactly what the doctor ordered.

Up next, Kentucky heads to Indianapolis to take on Indiana at Lucas Oil Stadium on Friday night.

articles.title: 3 takeaways after Kansas State basketball left no doubt vs Montana
articles.summary: Kansas State put together its most complete game of the season by blowing out Montana. Here are our takeaways.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — Kansas State basketball put together its most complete game of the young season in a beatdown of Montana.

The Wildcats cruised to an 86-45 win over the Grizzlies. It was K-State's third consecutive win after dropping their season opener.

New coach Casey Alexander's offense was humming as they continue to take steps forward, while more challenging opponents are on the horizon.

Here are our immediate takeaways from the win.

Kansas State basketball takes on Creighton

Kansas State basketball made it look easy vs Montana

There was never a doubt. The Wildcats did what a high-major should do to a mid-to-low-major.

Multiple extended scoring runs with solid play throughout the entire 40-minute game gave the Wildcats maybe their most complete game of the season, unless you want to count last week's win over Creighton.

The Wildcats shot 56.7% from the field, while Montana was held to 32.7%. Five different K-State players scored 10 or more points. It was a good night for the Cats.

It doesn't have to be the Brandon Rechsteiner show for the Wildcats

Brandon Rechsteiner, coming off back-to-back career-high 26-point games, didn't score in the first half and finished the night with 10 points.

Everyone on the floor contributed in some way. Isaiah Abraham led the team in scoring with 16 points. Timo Malovec, making his first K-State start, looked like the high-IQ player Alexander teased he'd be with smart passes and tough rebounds. He finished with 12 points, four assists and three rebounds.

Brock Vice also had a career night, recording his first double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds. His previous career-high on the boards was the seven he grabbed twice last season at Murray State.

Jaylen Alexander finished with five steals, the most by any freshman in K-State history.

Campbell visits Manhattan before Players Era

The Wildcats host Campbell on Friday, Nov. 20, for their last dress rehearsal before playing in the loaded Players Era tournament next week in Las Vegas. The first game pits them against Gonzaga on Nov. 24.

Campbell, out of the Coastal Athletic Association, is 1-3 after beating USC Upstate on Nov. 14. The Camels started their year with blowout losses to NC State, Western Michigan and East Tennessee State.

articles.title: Mitchell and Allen power the Cavaliers to a 126-115 win over the Bulls
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night.

Cleveland trailed by six points, 31-25, after one period before rebounding in the second. The Cavaliers used a 32-17 scoring edge in the second quarter for a 57-48 advantage at the break. Cleveland maintained its nine-point lead through the third quarter and weathered a fourth quarter comeback try by the Bulls to win for the third time in four games.

Tyrese Proctor scored 10 of his 17 points in the first half for Cleveland, which improved to 6-2 at home. Peyton Watson chipped in 14 points, Meleek Thomas added 10 and James Harden finished with nine points and 10 assists.

Norman Powell led Chicago with 27 points, and Matas Buzelis scored 23. Jalen Smith posted 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Tre Jones finished with 16 points and Isaac Okoro had 13.

The loss halted the Bulls' two-game win streak, which followed an eight-game skid. Chicago fell to 2-6 on the road and 3-10 overall.

The Cavaliers were without Evan Mobley, who has a sprained big toe on his right foot. Cleveland says he will be re-evaluated in seven to 10 days.

Bulls: At the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.

Cavaliers: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday.

articles.title: Dolphins waive kicker after costly missed field goals vs. Colts
articles.summary: One day after losing to the Indianapolis Colts, the Miami Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez.
articles.body:
One day after losing to the Indianapolis Colts , the Miami Dolphins waived kicker Zane Gonzalez.

This move comes after a rough outing for Gonzalez against the Colts .

In a game that the Colts won by only two points, Gonzalez missed an extra point attempt and two field goal attempts. Overall, he was 2-for-5 on kicks during Sunday's contest.

If he had made one of his two missed field goal attempts, the game may have ended differently.

Thanks to Gonzalez's missed kicks, the Colts were able to come away with their third win of the season.

Up next for Indianapolis is a Thursday night matchup with the Houston Texans .

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals RB James Conner could possibly return vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Head coach Mike LaFleur gave a promising update about veteran running back James Conner.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals might get a boost at running back this week. There is a possibility that James Conner, who has been on injured reserve all season, could come back.

Head coach Mike LaFleur said "it's trending well" when it comes to Conner's progress, noting he would have an update on Wednesday.

He even said "there's a chance" Conner could start in Week 11 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Conner hasn't played since Week 3 of last season, when he appeared to break his ankle.

The Cardinals could use the help at running back. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is on injured reserve and must miss at least two more games. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight combined for 34 rushing yards on Sunday.

We will see on Wednesday if Conner is designated to return and returns to practice for the first time since he was doing individual drills during training camp.

articles.title: Bane scores 24, Magic rally in 4th quarter to beat Celtics 115-105, extend win streak to 4 games
articles.summary: BOSTON (AP) — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory,...
articles.body:
BOSTON (AP) — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night.

Franz Wagner, who entered the night having scored 30 or more points in each of Orlando's previous four games, had 21 points, nine assists and eight rebounds. Anthony Black finished with 20 points and seven assists.

The Magic shot 50% (41 of 82) from the field in the game to earn their first win in Boston since Dec. 18, 2022.

It was Boston's first home loss of the season and snapped the team's six-game win streak. Jayson Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and 12 rebounds, his first double-double since their season-opening loss at Detroit. But he also had five of his team's 11 turnovers.

Paul George added 22 points and Payton Pritchard had 21 points.

The Magic, despite playing on three days of rest, struggled with their shot early. But they still managed to cobble together a 50-41 lead at halftime.

Playing on the second night of a back-to-back, the Celtics showed some early signs of fatigue. But they found some traction in the third quarter, led by Tatum's 14 points to outscore Orlando 36-25 in the period and take a 77-75 lead into the fourth.

But the Magic recovered and got an alley-oop from Wagner to Wendell Carter Jr., followed by a jumper by Bane to take a 110-99 edge with 1:33 left.

A night after finishing the first quarter with a franchise-high 33-point lead in its blowout win over Dallas, Boston needed a 3-pointer at the buzzer by Pritchard to even make it to 17 points by the end of the first period on Monday.

Both teams had trouble scoring in the opening quarter. The Magic went 7 of 21 (33.3%) from the field, while the Celtics made only 6 of 24 (25%) shots.

Magic: Host Philadelphia on Wednesday night.

Celtics: Visit Denver on Wednesday night.
